items.title: He said yes. He signs the cheques. It still never happened.
items.excerpt: A managing director agreed to change his entire fleet and nobody beat me to it. Twenty years later a £1.9M Aramco package started going the same way. What I did differently, and what I do on any deal that goes quiet.
items.author: Scott Robinson
items.body:
A managing director told me he wanted to change his entire fleet. Priced, specified, agreed. It never happened, and nobody beat me to it.

I was early in my career at Ford, selling contract hire. I had been taught to sell to the man who signs the cheque, so that is exactly what I did. His service team, his finance people and his management all had their own reasons to stay where they were. He was never going to make his own staff unhappy to please me.

Nobody beat me on that deal. I lost it on my own.

## It is not a rare way to lose

In a [2022 Harvard Business Review article](https://hbr.org/2022/06/stop-losing-sales-to-customer-indecision), Matthew Dixon and Ted McKenna report on more than 2.5 million recorded sales conversations. Between 40% and 60% of deals ended up lost to customers who expressed their intent to purchase and then failed to act. The study spans transactional and complex sales across the board rather than industrial sales in particular, and it comes from the authors' own book on the subject, so read it with that in mind.

Gartner asked buyers what goes on inside their buying groups. In a [survey of 632 B2B buyers, published in May 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process), 74% of buyer teams demonstrated unhealthy conflict during the decision. That is buyers reporting on themselves. In the same May 2025 release, Delainey Kirkwood of Gartner puts those groups at five to 16 people across as many as four functions.

That is the argument you are not in. It happens while you are sat at your desk waiting for an answer.

## Twenty years later, the same deal

Marjan Package 9. £1.9M, through Técnicas Reunidas, for Saudi Aramco. I inherited it late, after a sales restructure. Technical was signed off. The documentation was agreed. The terms were sat there going nowhere.

Same thing as the fleet deal. It looked done and it was not moving.

The difference was that by then I knew whose room the decision was actually in. So I stopped guessing at it through the contractor. I booked a call with Aramco and mapped the timings from the owner's side. Nobody else did that, because everybody else was working the EPC.

> Once I had the date the operator needed units on site, the deal had a spine.

I worked the lead time backwards from that date with Borja at Técnicas Reunidas. I ran the bonds and the legal in parallel instead of one after the other. It closed on the operator's on site date. Around 190 units.

I did not push harder than the Ford deal. I went and found out who the decision belonged to and what they actually needed.

## What to do on yours this week

Pick the one deal that has gone quiet and answer these on paper. This is [the decision map](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/#method) in its simplest form.

1. **Where does the decision actually live?** Not who signs. Who has to be comfortable before anybody signs. Write the names down. A question mark counts as an answer, and it tells you where to go next.
2. **Who is arguing against you, and what is their reason?** Most of the reasons belong to the business, not the person in front of you. Ask your contact who would be happiest if this never happened.
3. **What is in your champion's hands?** They are having that argument without you. Write them one page that answers the objections they will get.
4. **What is the real date?** Get it from the people who need the thing, not the people passing it on. Then work backwards through your lead time and show them the last day they can order.

If you cannot answer those, the deal has not stalled. You have lost sight of it.

## The short version

The man who signs is rarely the man who decides. Find the room, find who is arguing, and get the real date from the owner.

Got one that has stopped? [Bring a stalled deal](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/stalled-deal-review/). Thirty minutes on one deal, no charge, and you leave knowing where it has actually stopped and the three things to do next.

## Sources

- Harvard Business Review, "Stop Losing Sales to Customer Indecision", 2022. https://hbr.org/2022/06/stop-losing-sales-to-customer-indecision
- Gartner, "Gartner Sales Survey Finds 74% of B2B Buyer Teams Demonstrate Unhealthy Conflict During The Decision Process", 2025. https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process

items.title: We pushed into Caterpillar's engine build. They asked for an open book review.
items.excerpt: Technical gets you into the build. Quality decides whether you stay in it. Procurement decides whether you get paid. What that looked like at Caterpillar, GE and Saab, and how to run all three at once.
items.author: Scott Robinson
items.body:
I pushed to get into Caterpillar's engine build programme, and they asked for an open book review of our supply chain.

That is how you find out how many gates there are.

Technical gets you into the engine build. Quality decides whether you stay in it. Procurement decides whether you get paid. Win the first and lose either of the other two and you have worked eighteen months for nothing.

## What the gates look like on a real deal

I was at GG&G, Gilbert Gilkes & Gordon in Kendal, selling engine cooling pumps. Over the time I was there the business went from £2.5M to £15.2M, and the cycle came down from 18 to 24 months to around 12.

We started with Caterpillar's technical people, on marine engines. That was the easy part to enjoy. An engineer wants to talk about the product. You want to talk about the product. You can go home thinking it is going well.

Then the open book request landed. I pushed back. Eventually I yielded, but I presented it in a format that suited us. And behind that sat quality gateway after quality gateway, which was normal across most of our customers.

GE was the other side of the same coin. They sold few marine engines a year, big and low volume, so we wanted to charge for the design work. Around £150,000. I closed it. It was the first time in Gilkes' very long history that they had charged for pump design work. That was a commercial conversation, and technical could not have had it for me.

## Procurement is not waiting at the end

[Forrester's 2026 report on business buying](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/) says procurement professionals are decision makers in 53% of buying cycles and engage from the start of the process. That comes from a press release that does not state the sample or break it down by industry, so treat it as a direction rather than a measurement.

The same release puts the typical decision at 13 internal stakeholders and nine external influencers. [Delainey Kirkwood of Gartner, in a May 2025 release](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process), says five to 16 people across as many as four functions. Forrester lists outside influencers separately and that Gartner release does not say whether its figure includes them, so there is no single right number. The point is that it is a lot more people than the engineer you were talking to.

## Do not wait for the next gate

On Saab's naval programme in Sweden, a $650K multi stage tender, technical qualification and commercial negotiation ran at the same time. I ran them in parallel and stayed in front of the procurement decision makers at every stage rather than waiting for the next gate.

> Sequence is how sellers lose eighteen months. Run the gates side by side.

Treat them as three separate sales inside one deal. That is what [the decision map](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/#method) is for. Put a name against each gate this week, and ask each one a different question.

**Technical.** What do you need to see before you will put your name to it? Get the list in writing and agree it is the whole list.

**Quality.** What would make you take us out? Ask it while things are going well, and put your own quality person in front of theirs.

**Procurement.** What do you need in order to justify this? Not the discount. The justification. Then give it to them in their terms: total cost, risk and what a delay costs.

If you can only name the person at one of those gates, you know where to spend next week.

## The short version

Win all three gates or you have not won. Start all three early, and never let the engineer be your only friend in the building.

Got one that has stopped at a gate? [Bring a stalled deal](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/stalled-deal-review/). Thirty minutes on one deal, no charge, and you leave knowing where it has actually stopped and the three things to do next.

## Sources

- Forrester, "Forrester's 2026 Buyer Insights: GenAI Is Upending B2B Buying As Leaders Face Mounting Pressure To Justify Every Dollar Spent", 2026. https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/
- Gartner, "Gartner Sales Survey Finds 74% of B2B Buyer Teams Demonstrate Unhealthy Conflict During The Decision Process", 2025. https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process

items.title: Fifteen years in the ADNOC and Aramco specs. Somebody still had to sell it.
items.excerpt: Being specified is the biggest lever on a project. It is not the job. What I actually did to take Middle East sales up 167% in a year, what happened on 22 Bishopsgate, and five questions to ask before you walk away.
items.author: Scott Robinson
items.body:
Hughes were written into the ADNOC and Aramco specifications fifteen years before I joined. In 2024 I took Middle East sales up 167% on the year before.

I did not do that by getting into a specification. They were already in it.

Being specified is the single biggest lever in project sales. It tilts the odds hard in your favour and I would always rather be in than out. But a specification is a position, not an order. I am not going to tell you a story about those fifteen years, because I was not there. I can tell you what I did.

## What 167% actually took

I spent nine months out of twelve in the GCC that year. It was not a campaign. It was presence.

I removed the distributors that were no longer fit for purpose. The incumbent was a PPE distributor selling safety equipment, and that is a completely different sale. I spotted that the fire safety sector aligned far better and built a strong relationship there.

I got close to the EPC contractors in the region: Técnicas Reunidas, Samsung, Saipem, McDermott, Wood, CNPC, Tecnimont, Target Engineering.

Then I ran two prongs. Direct where we could, and bidding alongside the fire safety players where we could not. That mapped the market properly, and it opened up projects the business was never even getting to pitch for while it ran purely through distribution.

The reason matters. In a [2018 McKinsey survey of more than 100 senior US manufacturing executives](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/industrials/our-insights/the-coming-shakeout-in-industrial-distribution), manufacturers aiming for more direct sales gave developing more end customer relationships as their top reason, at 40% of respondents. Capturing the distributors' margins came in at 14%. That is US manufacturers in 2018, so read it with that in mind, but it is the right order of priorities. The relationship with the end customer comes first.

> Being written in gives you a position. Somebody still has to go and sell from it.

## Specified is where the work starts

22 Bishopsgate is a huge London tower. I was at Brannan, and the decision to specify our gauges and thermometers came from WSP. Job done, you would think.

It was not. We then had to give Multiplex, the main contractor, the confidence to use us. Hotchkiss, the MEP contractor, had to go with Wolseley, our partner, who held the relationship. So I worked with every business in the chain, the developers, WSP, Multiplex, Hotchkiss and Wolseley, and made sure every one of them knew who Brannan was.

I closed it before I had to ask for the business. When I did ask, I already knew we had it, because several people upstream had told me they were using us. Around £150,000, landed around August 2019.

## If you are outside it

It is not pass or fail. Thousands of projects are won by manufacturers who are on the approved vendor list and not written into the specification. It depends on the EPC, the operator, the budget and the commercial case.

Treat being outside the spec as the end of the job and you either walk away from winnable business or spend six months pushing at the wrong door.

On Marjan I booked a call with Aramco and mapped the timings from the owner's side. Nobody else did it, because everybody else was working the EPC. That is why [both angles](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/#method) is part of the method. The contractor will tell you what the specification says. The owner can tell you what they actually want and when they actually want it.

## Five questions before you walk away

1. Are you on the approved vendor list, or could you be in the time available?
2. Which EPC holds this, and how much room do they have?
3. What does the operator actually care about on this job?
4. Is there budget, and whose is it?
5. What is the commercial case for changing, stated in terms somebody can defend in a meeting you will not be in?

Some of the time those answers tell you to leave it alone, and that is a good result if you get it in a fortnight rather than a year.

## The short version

In the spec, go and sell from it. Out of it, find out before you walk. Either way, work every name in the chain.

Outside the spec on one right now? [Bring a stalled deal](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/stalled-deal-review/). Thirty minutes on one deal, no charge, and you leave knowing where it has actually stopped and the three things to do next.

## Sources

- McKinsey, "The coming shakeout in industrial distribution", 2019. https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/industrials/our-insights/the-coming-shakeout-in-industrial-distribution
